chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from a man from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A man forgot the Tawaf of the women (Tawaf al-Nisa') until he entered his wife. He said: 'Women are not permissible for him until he visits the House.'

And he said: 'He should order someone to perform it on his behalf if he has not yet performed Hajj. If he dies before being circumambulated for him, then his heir or another person should perform it on his behalf.'
And it is permissible for one who has circumambulated the House to delay the Sa'i to another time, and it is not permissible for him to delay it until the next day. Narrated.

key_terms.السَّعْيَ: Sa'i, the ritual walking between Safa and Marwah
key_terms.طَوَافَ النِّسَاءِ: Tawaf al-Nisa', the final circumambulation performed by men in Hajj
key_terms.يَزُورَ الْبَيْتَ: Visits the House (Kaaba), referring to performing the circumambulation
key_terms.يَقْضِ عَنْهُ: Performs it on his behalf / makes up for it

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a man forgets Tawaf al-Nisa' and has intercourse with his wife during Hajj?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the specific ruling for a man who forgets *Tawaf al-Nisa'* (the final circumambulation for men) and consummates marriage, prohibiting further intercourse until the ritual is completed or performed by proxy. It further establishes that while delaying *Sa'i* after *Tawaf* is permissible, it must occur within the same day, reflecting the structured temporal nature of Hajj rites. This highlights the Shia juristic emphasis on the validity of Hajj pillars being contingent upon their proper sequence and completion, even in cases of forgetfulness.
